Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : The first ionization enthalpy for oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen.

Reason R : The four electrons in 2p orbitals of oxygen experience more electron-electron repulsion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.content: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.

en.explanation:
In nitrogen () the three electrons occupy separate orbitals, while in oxygen () two of the four electrons must share one orbital.

The four electrons of oxygen therefore experience greater electron–electron repulsion, so the fourth electron is removed more easily than a electron of nitrogen; the first ionisation enthalpy of O (about ) is lower than that of N (about ).

Both A and R are correct, and the greater repulsion stated in R is the reason for A.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

en.content:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I : In CuSO4 . 5H2O, Cu-O bonds are present.

Statement II : In CuSO4 . 5H2O, ligands coordinating with Cu(II) ion are O-and S-based ligands.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.content: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

en.explanation:
In four water molecules are coordinated to through their oxygen atoms, giving ; the fifth water molecule is held by hydrogen bonds between a coordinated water molecule and the sulphate ion.

Cu–O coordinate bonds are therefore present, so Statement I is correct.

In the crystal the remaining two axial positions around Cu are taken by oxygen atoms of sulphate ions. The S atom of sulphate is bonded to four O atoms and carries no lone pair, so it never acts as a donor; every donor atom around is oxygen, and Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

en.explanation:
In 184 g of the compound: C , H , Br , so both isomers are .

Hot oxidises every side chain having a benzylic H to , so each isomer has one two-carbon side chain on the ring.

A gives benzoic acid, so Br is on the side chain; A is optically active, so the side chain carries a stereocentre: A . Being a secondary benzylic bromide, it ionises on warming with alcoholic and gives a pale yellow precipitate of AgBr.

B gives p-bromobenzoic acid, so Br is on the ring para to an ethyl group: B (achiral).

The o-methylbenzyl bromide in (A) and (B) is achiral and would give phthalic acid on oxidation.
